name: MUSA
aliases: Treatment for Mixed Urinary Incontinence: Midurethral Sling vs Botox A
question: Is intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA superior to a midurethral sling for overall symptoms in women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Outcome assessors masked; participants and surgeons unmasked
design.population: Women aged at least 21 years with moderate or severe bother from stress and urgency incontinence, a positive cough stress test, at least four urgency incontinence episodes on a three-day diary, and unsuccessful conservative and oral treatment; prior sling and anterior or apical prolapse at or beyond the hymen were excluded.
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Participants and Interventions and Randomization; Results: Study Population

verdictNote: OnabotulinumtoxinA did not meet the prespecified superiority test for six-month total UDI change.
takeaway: In women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U was not superior to synthetic mesh midurethral sling for six-month total UDI symptom improvement (mean difference 18.1 points, 95% CI −4.6 to 40.7; P=.12).

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.citation: Harvie HS, Menefee SA, Richter HE, et al. "Midurethral Sling vs OnabotulinumtoxinA in Females With Urinary Incontinence: The MUSA Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2025;333(21):1887-1896. doi:10.1001/jama.2025.4682
reports.followUp: Six-month primary outcome; exploratory follow-up through 12 months
